chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A Prophet from the children of Israel passed by a man whose body was half buried under a wall and half exposed; the exposed part had been pecked by birds and torn by dogs. Then he continued until he reached a city, and entered it, where he found one of its notables dead, lying on a bed covered with velvet, with censers around him. He said: 'O Lord, You are a Just Judge who does no injustice. That servant of Yours never associated a partner with You for even a blink of an eye, yet You caused him to die such a death. And this servant of Yours never believed in You for even a blink of an eye, yet You gave him such an honorable death.' Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) replied: 'My servant, I am indeed as you said—a Just Judge who does no injustice. That servant had a bad deed and a sin with Me, so I caused him to die that death so that he might meet Me with nothing left against him. And this servant had a good deed with Me, so I caused him to die that death so that he might meet Me with nothing left for him with Me (as reward).'

key_terms.الْمِيتَةُ: Death; specifically referring to the manner or state of dying
key_terms.طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ: A blink of an eye; a very short moment
key_terms.يُلْقَانِي: He may meet Me (in the Hereafter)

ai.seo_question: Why do righteous believers sometimes suffer humiliating deaths while disbelievers enjoy honorable ones?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the experience of a Prophet from the Children of Israel who observes two deaths: one of a faithful servant who suffered a humiliating death, and one of a disbeliever who enjoyed an honorable death. Allah explains that the humiliating death served to expiate the believer's remaining sins, while the honorable death served to preserve the disbeliever's good deeds for his future reward in the Hereafter.
